classification.difficultyReason: Recognise equal-side marks, calculate angles in two isosceles triangles and explain the different roles of the given angle.

content.prompt: Both of the triangles shown are isosceles.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2, left member of paired figures
spec.description: Downward-pointing isosceles triangle with a horizontal top side, matching single ticks on the sloping sides and three interior angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: The upper-left angle is 46 degrees, the upper-right angle is a and the bottom angle is b. The marked sloping sides are equal. Preserve source proportions without treating the drawing as an angle measurement.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 46-degree angle and unknown labels a and b are visible.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2, right member of paired figures
spec.description: Right-pointing isosceles triangle with a vertical left side, matching single ticks on the sides meeting at the right vertex and three interior angle arcs.
spec.mathematics: The upper-left angle is c, the lower-left angle is d and the right-hand angle is 46 degrees. The two marked sides meeting at the right vertex are equal. Preserve source proportions without treating the drawing as an angle measurement.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 46-degree angle and unknown labels c and d are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What part of the diagram tells you the triangles are isosceles?

answer.worked: The matching ticks show that two sides in each triangle are equal in length.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Determine the value of the missing angles $a, b, c, d$.

answer.worked:
Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, so $a=46^\circ$.

Using the angle sum of the first triangle:
$$\begin{align*}b+46+46&=180\\b+92&=180\\b&=88^\circ\end{align*}$$

In the second triangle, $c=d$. Using its angle sum:
$$\begin{align*}c+c+46&=180\\2c+46&=180\\2c&=134\\c&=67^\circ\\d&=67^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Explain why angles $a$ and $b$ are different to $c$ and $d$, even though both triangles have similar information.

answer.short: In the first triangle, $46^\circ$ is a base angle. In the second, it is the vertex angle between the equal sides.
answer.worked: In the first triangle, $46^\circ$ is one of the two equal base angles, so the other base angle is also $46^\circ$. In the second triangle, $46^\circ$ is the angle between the equal sides, so the two equal base angles share the remaining $134^\circ$.
